correct_answers.text: Managing altitude and airspeed
Achieving desired vertical flight path
Transitioning between flight profiles

question: In the context of energy management in flight, what roles do throttle and elevator inputs play?

correct_answers.text: Throttle affects the airplane's total mechanical energy.

wrong_answers.text: Throttle has no effect on altitude.

correct_answers.text: Regulates changes in total mechanical energy

question: What happens when the elevator is pulled back on the front side of the power required curve?

correct_answers.text: The airplane climbs briefly.

question: What is the effect of pushing the elevator forward on the backside of the power required curve?

correct_answers.text: The airplane accelerates.
Airspeed increases.
Total drag is reduced.

question: What are two major risks associated with mismanagement of energy in flight according to the Airplane Flying Handbook?

correct_answers.text: Unwanted deviations from the desired energy state
Unintentional, irreversible deceleration
Unintentional sink rate causing depletion of mechanical energy

question: What actions should a pilot take to correct an unintentional descent below the desired glideslope on final approach?

correct_answers.text: Pitch up
Throttle up

question: What actions can a pilot take to prevent a crash when flying toward rising terrain?

correct_answers.text: Increase climb rate to gain altitude.
Execute a 180-degree turn to avoid terrain.
Use maximum power to enhance climb performance.

wrong_answers.text: Continue on the same heading without adjustments.
Wait for ATC instructions before taking action.
Reduce climb rate to save engine wear.

correct_answers.text: Total energy errors
